clips.selection_note: Body-driven cut and low load through frame 22, then complete original-character planted recovery and slow rise from high-catch-v17/high-rise-v21. No mixed body segments or per-frame recentering; steel follows the source grip with recorded local repair.

root_motion.method: v26 physical step finishes at frame 15. v27 uses complete in-place body poses through recovery; no stitched legs or upper-body recentering. Source extraction is zero; world advance stays fixed during recovery.

clips.selection_note: Approved forward thrust and return, 64 uniformly timed frames with loaded/contact holds. Source order and cumulative millisecond timing are preserved.

chroma_note: Base green dominance >64 preserves tinted steel. pipeline.assembly: ffv1 RGB lossless, decoded frames checked against original source parts
pipeline.output_resize: 512x384 nearest; source RGB retained except recorded local steel repairs in pixel-corrections.json
pipeline.runtime_timing: 64 uniform SpriteFrames entries per clip. Runtime FPS is 64/full duration; editable Aseprite/APNG use cumulative millisecond boundary rounding.
pipeline.combo: Each equipped stance currently uses entry -> one complete attack Timeline -> finished. Generic input-window/consume branching remains available and tested with an in-memory combo graph.
pipeline.matte_corrections: Aseprite applies the exact erase/restore coordinates; package verifies full expected RGBA, all unchanged retained RGB, atlas, APNG and continuation endpoints.

reference_design.high: Official Monster Hunter greatsword load, descending cut and knee/hip catch. Retains clean approved strike poses and newly stages low elbow fold/hilt retraction before rising back to high guard.
reference_design.mid: LIER horizontal-cut mechanics: coiled pelvis/ribs, coordinated turn and front-leg weight transfer, one continuous waist-height blade arc with an edge-aligned follow-through.
reference_design.low: Wapenkunst rules 4-5: elbow-led hilt retraction and stable point-forward thrust; rear-foot drive, then recovery along the same line.
reference_design.character: Eula official movement rhythm as a balance and step reference, adapted to this same young fox swordswoman with continuous two-handed grip.

weapon_attack_effects: Removed: animation-only attacks; stance-switch effects remain separate.
authoring_steps: Use the approved character and weapon. High uses body-driven cut, coherent planted recovery and slow rise; middle uses a forward horizontal cut with continuous recovery; low uses the approved thrust.
Select forward source poses from source_parts and retain exact canonical idle endpoints; each attack has 64 frames.
Apply recorded Aseprite matte and steel edits, preserving the source body, grip and foreground occlusion. Do not splice upper/lower bodies or recenter each pose.
High physics advance finishes at frame 15 during the downstroke. The source-image offset curve is independent from the runtime curve; recovery stays at the contact position.
Verify source RGBA plus pixel corrections, independent Aseprite exports, atlas/APNG, Godot import and both-facing player playback.

keypose_source_videos.use: Key extraction only; rejected for direct playback because of blade trail or looping return.

stability_revision.method: Use coherent complete original-character planted recovery poses, with original hands and body retained together; reuse the same idle steel master for blade consistency. Remove the stitched lower body and frame-by-frame upper-body offsets.
stability_revision.phase: low load -> elbow fold -> slow rise -> original idle
